confirmed_findings.title: New units are immune to their own entry bar: stops, TPs, trailing, and the intrabar FTMO guard are all evaluated before entries
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:603-733 (guard 603-621 and per-unit exits 625-688 run before entries 701-733; unit appended at 554-571 is first risk-checked at bar index+1)
confirmed_findings.claim: Within each bar iteration, the account-guard adverse-equity check and the per-unit stop/TP1/TP2/trail loop run BEFORE the entry blocks, and nothing re-checks a unit opened this bar. A position entered at bar[i].open is never tested against bar[i]'s low/high: an intrabar move through its 2.5-ATR stop is invisible until bar i+1 (where it books at the original stop price), and the unit contributes nothing to that bar's adverse_equity used for max_daily_loss_pct, official_breach, and soft_guard flattening (only the end-of-bar close mark at lines 749-762 sees it). The live EA has a broker-side SL active from the entry tick and runs ManagePositions per tick (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:1018-1022), so entry-bar stop-outs and entry-bar drawdown are real in live trading.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Entry-bar stop-outs are deferred, which can only match or improve the booked outcome (later fill at the same stop price, or survival if the next bar's low never returns to the stop); entry-bar adverse excursion is excluded from the max-daily-loss and rule-breach metrics, so the headline FTMO-compliance results (max_daily_equity_loss_pct, official_rule_breach, soft_guard_exits) are one-sidedly understated on exactly the news-spike bars the guard exists for. A partially offsetting effect exists (entry-bar TP1 hits are also deferred, which can only hurt), so trade P&L bias is mixed, but the compliance metrics are strictly flattered.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Verified by tracing the bar loop in ftmo_quant_backtest.py. Within each bar iteration the order is: flatten checks (593-601), FTMO guard adverse-equity (603-622), per-unit stop/TP1/TP2/trail (625-688), THEN entries (701-733, unit appended in try_open at 554-571). Nothing after the entry blocks re-tests a just-opened unit against that bar's high/low; the end-of-bar block (749-763) marks it at close only and never checks official_floor (official_breach is set only at 616-617 inside the pre-entry guard). So a unit filled at bar[i].open is first stop-checked at bar i+1 (line 627, booked at unit.stop) — deferral books the same stop price later or lets a spike-and-recover stop-out survive, never worse for the stop leg — and the entry bar's low/high never enters adverse_equity, max_daily_loss_pct, official_breach, or the soft-guard flatten. The live EA attaches the SL broker-side at order send (FTMOQuantEA.mq5 lines 704/712) and runs CheckAccountGuard/ManagePositions every tick (OnTick 1018-1022), so entry-bar stop-outs and drawdown are real live. This is not a disclosed limitation (docstring lines 4-9 and metadata line 815 cover H1 granularity, stop-first pessimism, constant spread — not entry-bar immunity), and it is not inherent to bar-level simulation since the fill is at the open, making same-bar checking fully causal. Minor quibble: "strictly flattered" has a rare offsetting edge case (deferred entry-bar TP1 leaves full lots/original stop exposed to bar i+1's guard, which can overstate that bar's adverse equity), but the core mechanism — entry-bar adverse excursion excluded from the compliance metrics and entry-bar stop-outs deferred at same-or-better booking — is concretely correct at the cited lines. Claim stands; direction (inflates compliance results, mixed on trade P&L) is accurate.

confirmed_findings.title: HTF confluence is evaluated one H1 bar early, making the H4 filter a full extra H4 bar stale at bucket-boundary hours (including 08:00 session open)
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:420-431 (prev = index-1) combined with 244-248 (aligned arrays already hold bucket-1)
confirmed_findings.claim: htf_fast_al[i] already stores the EMA of the last completed HTF bucket relative to bar i (bucket(i)-1). context_ok then reads htf_fast_al[prev] with prev = index-1, i.e. bucket(index-1)-1. Whenever bar index opens a new H4 bucket (hours 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 — of which 8 and 16 are tradable session hours, hour 8 being the first tradable hour of the session), bucket(index-1) = bucket(index)-1, so the filter uses bucket(index)-2: one full H4 bar older than both the docstring's 'last completed HTF bar' contract (lines 225-227) and the EA, which reads shift 1 on the H4 chart at signal time (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:532-539) and would see the just-completed 04:00-08:00 bar at an 08:00 entry. The correct index is htf_fast_al[index], which is still causal. The D1 stack is unaffected in practice because session-hour bars never open a new calendar-day bucket.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Not look-ahead (it errs in the stale direction), but the backtest admits/rejects a different trade set than the EA at 2 of the 8 tradable hours: it can take breakouts the EA's fresh H4 stack would veto and veto ones the EA would take. Trade-population divergence from the mirrored EA, with no systematic flattering direction.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Verified by concrete execution tracing: (1) Decision moment is the open of bar `index` — try_open fills at bar.open (ftmo_quant_backtest.py:527-530) and signal() reads bars[index-1] as the completed breakout bar (262-265), matching the EA's new-bar shift-1 evaluation. (2) htf_ema_aligned already embeds the one-bar shift: fast_aligned[i] = htf_fast[bucket(i)-1] (244-248), per the docstring contract (225-227). (3) context_ok then reads htf_fast_al[prev] with prev = index-1 (420-422), i.e. htf_fast[bucket(index-1)-1]. Mid-bucket this equals htf_fast_al[index] (no divergence), but when bar index opens a new H4 bucket (hour // 4 boundary: hours 0,4,8,12,16,20; line 232), bucket(index-1) = bucket(index)-1, so the filter evaluates bucket(index)-2 — one full H4 bar staler than the EA, which reads shift 1 on H4 at signal time (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:532-539) and at 08:00 sees the just-completed 04:00-08:00 bar. With Config session_start=8/session_end=17/skip_hours=(12,) the tradable hours are 8,9,10,11,13,14,15,16, of which 8 and 16 are boundaries — exactly 2 of 8, and hour 8 is the session's first tradable hour. htf_fast_al[index] is the correct index and is still causal (bucket(index)-1 is complete at bar index's open). The D1 caveat also holds: with continuous 24h data a 00:00 bar exists, so no tradable-hour bar starts a new day bucket. The other prev-based gates (ATR regime 437-443, market structure 444-457) correctly mirror the EA's shift-1 reads; the double shift is specific to the pre-shifted HTF arrays. Not a disclosed limitation — the code's own comments (227, 401-402) assert the arrays reference the last completed HTF bar at evaluation time, which prev-indexing violates at boundary hours. Impact direction as claimed: stale (not look-ahead), so neutral/unknown trade-population divergence from the mirrored EA — it can both admit trades the EA's fresh H4 stack would veto and veto trades the EA would take; infrequent in practice with slow 50/200 EMA stacks but a genuine parity defect.

confirmed_findings.title: Pullback arming runs on every bar, but the EA only folds bars seen through its session/loss/new-bar gates — the backtest's pyramid adds do not correspond to live behavior
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:736-744 (unconditional arming block) vs FTMOQuantEA.mq5:1046-1060 (UpdatePullback reached only after accountSafe, IsTradingSession, daily-loss-cap, and new-bar gates) and mq5:461-462 (only shift-1 is ever folded, so skipped bars are lost permanently)
confirmed_findings.claim: The backtest updates trend_extreme and arms pullback re-entries on every bar while units are open, including the 15 out-of-session hours (17:00-07:00), the hour-12 skip, and bars after the daily loss cap trips. The EA calls UpdatePullback only on the first tick of a new bar that survives the session and loss gates, and it folds only the shift-1 bar, so highs/lows of gated-out bars (e.g. every overnight bar except 07:00, and the 11:00 bar hidden behind the 12:00 skip) never enter its extreme tracking and can never arm a re-entry. The backtest will therefore arrive at 08:00 already armed from overnight pullbacks the live EA cannot see, and measures pullback depth from deeper extremes.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: No future data is used (arming is consumed next bar), but the pyramid-add path — a core strategy component after TP1 — fires on a different, generally more frequent schedule than the live EA. Backtested pyramid frequency, add prices, and their P&L contribution are not what the EA will produce live; direction of the P&L error is unknown.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed by concrete trace of both files. Backtest ftmo_quant_backtest.py:736-747 folds every H1 bar's high/low into trend_extreme and sets pullback_armed whenever units are open (guards are only `units and trend_side != 0 and isfinite(atr)`), including the 15 out-of-session hours, the hour-12 skip, and post-loss-cap bars — the block sits outside entry_ready. The EA (FTMOQuantEA.mq5) reaches UpdatePullback only at line 1060, behind the accountSafe/IsTradingSession return (1046-1047), the daily-loss-cap return (1051-1052), and the new-bar gate (1054-1057); lastSignalBar is assigned only at 1057, after those returns, so it does not advance during gated hours, and UpdatePullback (453-484) reads only shift-1 (iHigh/iLow(...,1)). Grep confirms no other call site and OnTimer (1011-1016) never folds. Concrete execution: overnight ticks 17:00-07:59 return at 1046; at the first 08:00 tick shift-1 = the 07:00 bar only, so bars 16:00-06:00 are permanently lost to extreme tracking; likewise the 11:00 bar is lost behind the 12:00 skip (at 13:00, shift-1 = 12:00). Positions do carry overnight in both engines, so these bars matter. In-session timing is identical on both sides (bar N-1 folded before the add decision at bar N's open), so the claim correctly reports no lookahead — it is a parity divergence: backtest arming is a strict superset of live arming (superset of folded bars, >= tracked extreme), so pyramid adds fire more frequently and from deeper measured pullbacks than the live EA can produce. This is not among the disclosed limitations (H1 granularity, constant spread, server-time timestamps, stop-first pessimism); the docstring explicitly claims to mirror the EA's session logic. Refutation attempts (lastSignalBar catching up, other fold paths, shift-1 capturing the overnight range, disclosed-limitation framing) all fail on the cited lines. Direction of the P&L error is genuinely unknown (depends on whether the extra adds are net-positive), matching the claim's neutral_or_unknown label.

confirmed_findings.title: Break-even stop after TP1 is never enforced within the TP1 bar (runner gets a free pass on same-bar retraces)
confirmed_findings.claim: When TP1 hits, line 644 sets unit.stop = unit.entry inside the same loop iteration. The only same-bar exit path afterwards is the trail block, but line 684 requires `candidate != unit.stop` to book, and candidate equals the just-set break-even stop (entry), so it can never fire. Result: a bar whose high reaches TP1 (+1R) and whose low then retraces to/below entry leaves the 60% runner alive into the next bar. The live EA manages per tick (FTMOQuantEA.mq5 lines 807-851): the instant TP1 fills it moves the SL to open, so any subsequent same-bar tick at/below entry stops the runner at break-even. The same gap applies after a same-bar TP2 whenever the trail level sits below entry.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: On wide-range bars (range >= 1R = 2.5 ATR + spread — exactly the violent reversal bars where BE protection matters live) the backtest's runner survives and can go on to book TP2/trail profits that the live EA's break-even stop would have cut to ~0. Where the next bar does dip to entry the fill price is identical (just delayed), so the divergence is one-sided: the backtest can only do better than live, never worse. This directly contradicts the module docstring's 'intrabar ambiguity is resolved against the strategy' claim — the ambiguous high-first-vs-low-first path is resolved in the strategy's favor here.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
The claim is CONFIRMED by concrete code reading; I could not refute it on any ground.

Mechanics verified in C:/Users/Sanique Richards/Documents/Homework Heroes/Pokemon/Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:
(1) Line 644 sets `unit.stop = unit.entry` directly inside the TP1 branch (lines 641-647), within the same per-unit loop iteration.
(2) The only remaining same-bar exit path is the trail block (lines 662-688). For a long after TP1 (tp2_done False), `candidate` starts as `unit.stop` (= entry, line 665); the break-even branch (666-671) computes `max(entry, entry)` = entry; the trail branch (672-680) is gated on `unit.tp2_done` so it cannot raise candidate. Thus `candidate == unit.stop` always, and line 684's `retraced and candidate != unit.stop` can never be true — the runner cannot be booked in the TP1 bar even when `bar.low <= entry`. Symmetric for shorts. The claim's TP2 corollary also checks out: after a same-bar TP2, candidate = max(entry, trail), so whenever the trail level sits at/below entry, candidate again equals unit.stop and no same-bar BE exit is possible.
(3) The next-bar stop check (lines 626-631) books at `unit.stop` = entry, so where the next bar does dip to entry the fill price is identical (delayed only); where it doesn't, the backtest keeps a runner that per-tick management could have BE-stopped. Since the runner's stop is pinned at entry, subsequent exits are at entry or better (TP2/trail), making the divergence one-sided in the strategy's favor — INFLATES, as alleged. (Only a rare gap-through-entry on a flatten bar could hurt; negligible and doesn't change the direction.)

Live-EA contrast verified in C:/Users/Sanique Richards/Documents/Homework Heroes/Pokemon/Bot-EA/experts/FTMOQuantEA.mq5: ManagePositions() is called from OnTick() every tick (lines 1018-1022). On the TP1 tick (lines 807-823) it books the partial and immediately sets flags=1; the same tick's SL block (lines 843-851) computes candidate = MathMax(sl, open) for flags >= 1 and modifies the broker-side SL to breakeven (subject only to minStopDistance, which is satisfied at the +1R TP1 price). Any subsequent same-bar tick at/below entry then stops the runner at ~breakeven. So the alleged backtest-vs-live gap is real.

Not a disclosed limitation: the module docstring (lines 6-8) explicitly promises "Intrabar ambiguity is resolved against the strategy (stop before target; triggered trailing stops may fill in the same bar)". The trail-booking mechanism (`candidate != unit.stop` at line 684) was clearly designed to let intrabar-moved stops fill same-bar, but the TP1 break-even move bypasses it by mutating `unit.stop` at line 644 before the trail block reads it — so this specific ambiguity is resolved FOR the strategy, contradicting the harness's own stated convention. This is a genuine correctness defect, not H1-granularity/constant-spread/stop-first pessimism as disclosed.

Verdict: not refuted — the finding stands as an INFLATES-results defect.

confirmed_findings.title: Stops fill at exact stop price even when the bar opens/gaps beyond the stop — including at prices the bar never traded
confirmed_findings.location: C:/Users/Sanique Richards/Documents/Homework Heroes/Pokemon/Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py lines 626-631 (amplified by aggregate_h1 lines 165-166)
confirmed_findings.claim: stop_hit is `bar.low <= unit.stop` (long) / `bar.high + spread >= unit.stop` (short) and always books at unit.stop. If the bar opens through the stop (news gap, or a data hole — aggregate_h1 silently drops any hour missing one of its four M15 candles, so consecutive 'H1' bars can be many hours apart), the live broker SL fills at the open, which is strictly worse. In the extreme case (bar.high < unit.stop for a long), the engine books a fill at a price the bar never traded at all. confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Every gap-through-stop loss is understated by (stop - open) [long] on the full remaining lots; the runner's ratcheted trail stop is also filled at its exact level across gaps. Magnitude is bounded because the Friday>=17:00 flatten avoids most weekend holds, but intraday news gaps and dropped-hour data holes remain, and the error is one-directional (losses can only be understated, never overstated).
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed at the cited lines. ftmo_quant_backtest.py lines 626-631: stop_hit is `bar.low <= unit.stop` (long) / `bar.high + spread >= unit.stop` (short) and the exit always books via `book(unit, unit.stop, ...)` — there is no clamp to bar.open. The error is one-directional: gap-through losses are always understated, never overstated — it inflates results. The claim accurately characterizes the code and its impact; not refuted.

confirmed_findings.title: Trailing stop uses the current bar's ATR (atr[index]) — intrabar look-ahead and parity mismatch with the EA's shift-1 ATR
confirmed_findings.location: C:/Users/Sanique Richards/Documents/Homework Heroes/Pokemon/Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py lines 672-677 (also 736-743 for pullback arming)
confirmed_findings.claim: The trail level is `bar.high - atr[index] * trail_atr`, where atr[index] is the Wilder ATR *including the current bar's full true range* — a value not knowable at any intrabar moment when the fill is deemed to occur (line 685 books a same-bar exit at this level). The EA trails per tick using IndicatorValue(atrHandle, 1) — the last *completed* bar's ATR (FTMOQuantEA.mq5 line 739, 855-857). So the backtest both feeds future information into a same-bar fill price/decision and systematically diverges from the EA: on the wide-range bars where same-bar trail exits fire, atr[index] > atr[index-1], making the backtest trail looser than the live trail.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: A looser trail moves the fill lower (worse for a long) when it does fire, but also makes the exit less likely to fire at all, letting the runner ride further — net sign depends on subsequent path. Given this program was just burned by a non-causal harness input, any intrabar decision fed by the bar's own completed range should be flagged regardless of direction. Fix is one character-class: use atr[index-1] for the trail (and for pullback arming, though that one is bar-close-causal already).
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. (1) atr[index] includes bar[index]'s own true range: wilder_atr (ftmo_quant_backtest.py lines 190-205) folds the current bar's TR into output[index], and the engine's own causal convention proves the offset (entries use atr[index-1] at line 531; signal/filters use index-1 throughout). Non-causal input, exactly the artifact class the program was burned by. (3) EA parity mismatch verified: FTMOQuantEA.mq5 line 739 uses IndicatorValue(atrHandle, 1) — the last completed bar's ATR — applied per tick at lines 855/857; during a forming bar that corresponds to atr[index-1] in the backtest, not atr[index]. Even the non-fill path (line 688 ratchets unit.stop into the next bar) diverges from the EA's intrabar ratchet. (4) Not covered by disclosures: the docstring discloses same-bar trailing-stop fills as deliberate pessimism, but says nothing about the ATR input choice; the shift error is a separate, undocumented defect. (5) Direction as claimed: on the wide-range bars where same-bar trail exits fire, atr[index] > atr[index-1] typically, making the backtest trail looser than live — lower fill when it fires but fewer fires, so net sign is path-dependent (neutral_or_unknown is a fair label). Fix as claimed: use atr[index-1] at lines 674/676 (and 739/743 for pullback arming for strict EA parity, though that one is already bar-close-causal since pullback_armed is only consumed on the next bar's entry).

confirmed_findings.title: Entry-bar exposure escapes the intrabar guard and stop processing entirely
confirmed_findings.claim: The adverse-equity guard block (lines 603-622) and the per-unit stop/TP loop (lines 625-688) both run BEFORE the entry blocks (lines 701-733). A unit opened by try_open at bar.open (line 528) is exposed to that bar's full H1 range, but neither its 2.5-ATR stop nor its contribution to adverse_equity is evaluated against that bar's low/high; the first check happens on the NEXT bar using next-bar extremes. Only the close-of-bar equity mark (lines 749-763) sees the new unit. The EA it mirrors checks equity and manages exits on every tick (FTMOQuantEA.mq5 OnTick lines 1018-1022), so entry-bar intrabar management exists live.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Same-bar stop-outs are silently skipped: if the entry bar spikes through the stop and the next bar opens back inside, the harness stays in a trade the EA would have stopped out, converting live losses into backtest survivals. For the FTMO metrics, the entry bar's adverse excursion of every new unit (initial entries AND pyramid adds) is invisible to max_daily_loss_pct, the soft-guard flatten, and official_breach - a within-entry-bar daily/total floor touch is never flagged. Bounded per unit (~0.35% risk sized) but systematic across every position's first bar, and pyramid adds occur exactly when aggregate exposure is highest.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Execution order in run_backtest's per-bar loop (ftmo_quant_backtest.py:574-763) is exactly as claimed: the adverse-equity FTMO guard (603-622) and the per-unit stop/TP/trail loop (625-688) both iterate `units` BEFORE the entry blocks (701-709 new trend, 711-733 pyramid) append new units via try_open at bar.open (528). A unit opened this bar is therefore never checked against this bar's low/high: its 2.5-ATR stop is first evaluated next bar against next-bar extremes (so an entry-bar spike through the stop followed by a next-bar open back inside survives in the backtest), and its entry-bar adverse excursion is invisible to max_daily_loss_pct (612-615), official_breach (616-617), and the soft-guard flatten (618-622). Refutation attempts fail: (1) not the disclosed H1-OHLC/stop-first limitation — entry is at bar.open so the whole bar range is causally post-entry and could be checked; the docstring (lines 6-8) promises ambiguity resolved AGAINST the strategy, and this gap resolves it FOR the strategy; (2) try_open's projected-risk gate (543-547) is a sizing check at the open, not an excursion check — max_daily_loss_pct elsewhere deliberately marks at bar.low, which can exceed the stop distance; (3) EA parity is accurate — FTMOQuantEA.mq5 OnTick (1018-1022) runs CheckAccountGuard/ManagePositions every tick, and OpenUnit attaches a broker-side SL at entry (trade.Buy(..., sl, ...) line 704, mirror 712), so live the same-bar stop-out is guaranteed by the server. confirmed_findings.title: Projected-risk pyramid gate uses realized balance where the EA uses live equity
confirmed_findings.claim: Harness: projected = balance - (open_risk() + risk_money) * 1.15 (line 543). EA: projectedEquity = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_EQUITY) - (OpenRiskMoney() + riskMoney) * 1.15 (EA lines 435-436). Balance excludes floating PnL of open units, equity includes it, so the two gates admit different pyramid adds. Pyramid adds require any(unit.tp1_done) (line 718) and surviving post-TP1 runners have stop>=entry (line 644) and bar.low above it, i.e. positive floating at add time - so the harness gate is usually TIGHTER than the EA's; with underwater pre-TP1 units in the book it flips LOOSER.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: The backtest systematically models a different pyramiding cadence than the EA it claims to mirror: in the typical floating-profit case it takes fewer adds than the EA would (understating both the EA's live exposure/breach risk and, if adds are profitable, its returns); in the floating-loss case it permits adds the EA would refuse. Net direction on headline results depends on add profitability in the tested period, but guard statistics (soft_guard_exits, official_breach, max_daily_loss_pct) no longer describe the EA's actual behavior.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. The cited code is exactly as claimed on both sides. Harness (Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py line 543): `projected = balance - (open_risk() + risk_money) * 1.15`, where `balance` is the realized-only ledger (updated exclusively in `book()`, line 484, on closes; floating PnL of open units is never in it — the harness computes mark-to-market equity separately at lines 749-753, so this was a choice, not a model constraint). EA (experts/FTMOQuantEA.mq5 lines 435-437): `projectedEquity = AccountInfoDouble(ACCOUNT_EQUITY) - (OpenRiskMoney() + riskMoney) * 1.15`, and ACCOUNT_EQUITY includes floating PnL. Both EA entry paths route through this equity gate: fresh entries at line 1067 and pyramid adds at line 1093 both call OpenUnit, which calls ProjectedRiskAllowed at line 693. In the harness, both paths (lines 705, 731) call try_open with the balance-based gate at line 543. The divergence is inert when flat (balance == equity with no open units), so it manifests exactly and only on pyramid adds, as the claim says. The directional analysis also checks out: an add requires any(unit.tp1_done) (harness line 718), a TP1-done unit has stop moved to entry (line 644) and must have survived this bar's stop check (bar.low > stop >= entry for longs), so that unit's floating PnL is positive at add time — equity > balance — meaning the EA's gate is looser and the harness refuses adds the EA would take; with underwater pre-TP1 add units in the book the sign can flip. Refutation angles all fail: (1) it is not among the disclosed limitations (H1 OHLC granularity, constant spread, server-time timestamps, stop-first pessimism) — the docstring at lines 4-8 affirmatively claims to mirror the EA's 'sizing ... and FTMO guard logic', and the comment at lines 541-542 presents the gate as the EA's; (2) it is not forced by the bar-level model, since the harness already marks equity to bar prices elsewhere (lines 605-611, 749-753); (3) materiality is honestly bounded by the claim itself (P2, neutral/unknown headline direction) and the fidelity of guard statistics (soft_guard_exits, official_breach, max_daily_loss_pct) is genuinely affected since the gate changes which adds occur. A compounding (unclaimed but corroborating) detail: the harness also sizes risk_money from balance (line 534) where the EA sizes from ACCOUNT_EQUITY (lines 691-692), i.e. the balance-for-equity substitution is systematic at add time, which reinforces rather than undermines the finding.

confirmed_findings.title: R denominator uses padded risk budget, not dollars actually risked — a full stop-out books ~-0.91R, never -1R
confirmed_findings.claim: book() prorates unit_risk from risk_budget (= balance*risk_pct/100, line 534) by close_lots/original_lots, but lots were sized as (risk_money/sizing_cost_reserve)/(initial_risk*dppl) then floor_volume'd (lines 535-538), so actual dollars at risk to the initial stop are at most risk_budget/1.10 and further reduced by step flooring. Every trade's r (line 500) is therefore scaled toward zero by ~9-15%: a full initial-stop loss reports r ~= -0.909 minus commission (~-0.93R), and wins are shrunk by the same factor.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: expectancy_r (summarize line 360) systematically understates true per-dollar-risked R by the cost-reserve factor plus flooring slack. For a positive-edge screen the headline expectancy_r is understated ~10%+; symmetric shrink also makes a losing strategy look closer to zero. R-based hurdle comparisons (e.g. 'losses are -1R') are miscalibrated.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed at the cited lines. try_open sizes lots as (risk_money/1.10)/(initial_risk*dppl) then floors to volume_step (lines 534-538), yet stores the un-shrunk risk_money as Position.risk_budget (line 565, field order lines 46-48). book() sets unit_risk = risk_budget prorated by close_lots/original_lots (487-491) and r = pnl/unit_risk (500). Stops fill exactly at unit.stop with no slippage (631), so the largest gross loss realizable on the initial stop is lots*initial_risk*dppl <= risk_money/1.10 (minus flooring slack), giving gross r = -0.909 on a full stop-out, never -1; commission then shifts it slightly. Wins shrink by the identical 1/1.10 factor (a tp1_r=1.0 partial books +0.909R gross). summarize (line 360) averages these uncorrected r values into expectancy_r. Refutation attempts fail: initial_risk (actual priced risk) is stored but never used as the denominator; the module's disclosed limitations (lines 2-9: H1 granularity, stop-first pessimism, etc.) do not cover the R-denominator convention; with commission_per_side = 0 (metas without usd_per_lot, lines 385-390) the 10% pad is pure denominator inflation, not a cost reserve realized in the accounting. The claim's mechanics, cited lines, and impact (expectancy_r magnitude understated ~9-15%, R-hurdle calibration broken, symmetric shrink pulls losers toward zero) are all accurate; only the illustrative "~-0.93R" figure depends on commission magnitude, which the claim already qualifies. Not refutable.

confirmed_findings.title: Swap/overnight financing entirely unmodeled despite multi-week runner holds; the EA's own accounting includes DEAL_SWAP
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:482-483 (book pnl = gross - commission only); holds allowed overnight, only Friday flatten at 600-601
confirmed_findings.claim: book() computes pnl as gross minus commission only; no swap/rollover term exists anywhere in the file. Positions are held across nights all week (weekend flatten only, line 600) and runners trail for days/weeks until an EMA flip. The mirrored EA explicitly folds DEAL_SWAP into its daily PnL and loss counting (FTMOQuantEA.mq5 lines 260, 292), so live results will include a cost the harness never charges. This is not in the disclosed-limitations list (docstring lines 4-9 and the 'model' string at line 815 mention only OHLC granularity, spread fallback, timezone, stop-first pessimism).
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Long-held runner trades — the profit engine of this trend design — accrue zero holding cost in the harness. Sign depends on side and rate differential, but omitted swap (including triple-swap days) typically flatters multi-week FX holds; dollar PnL, PF and the FTMO daily-loss/guard path are all measured without this drag.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: The core defect is real and grounded at the cited lines, so the claim stands (with one magnitude-level correction). Verified concretely: (1) book() at ftmo_quant_backtest.py:477-505 computes pnl = side*(exit-entry)*dollars_per_price minus 2*commission_per_side*close_lots only (lines 482-483); a case-insensitive grep for swap/rollover/financing over the whole file returns zero hits, so no overnight financing term exists anywhere in the harness. (2) Positions genuinely carry overnight: in_session() gates only entry_ready (line 690-698), never forces exits, and the only calendar flatten is the Friday >= friday_close one at lines 600-601, so a unit opened Monday can hold through 4 rollover nights (including the FX Wednesday triple-swap, i.e. up to ~6 swap-nights of financing per hold). (3) The mirrored EA does fold DEAL_SWAP into both its day-start balance anchor (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:157), its daily PnL (line 260), and its per-deal loss counting for the max-losses-day guard (line 292) — so live daily-loss/guard behavior and live PnL include a cost the harness never charges, meaning the harness is not merely omitting a cost but also diverging from the EA's own guard arithmetic it claims to mirror. (4) It is not a disclosed limitation: the docstring (lines 2-9) discloses only conservative intrabar/stop-first resolution, and the model/source strings (lines 815, 816-822) disclose OHLC screening, spread fallback, and the timezone assumption — swap appears nowhere. One correction to the claim's framing: 'multi-week runner holds' is wrong — the Friday flatten the claim itself cites caps every hold at under 5 calendar days, so materiality is per-week-capped (roughly a few dollars to a few tens of dollars per lot per held week on EURUSD), smaller than the 'multi-week drag' narrative implies. That overstates impact but does not refute the defect: swap is unmodeled, holds do cross nights, the EA counts swap, and it is undisclosed. Sign is genuinely side/rate-differential dependent (the claim concedes this); with retail swap markups it is typically a net drag, so 'inflates (mildly)' is a fair characterization, but 'unknown-sign, likely mildly inflating' would be the precise label.

confirmed_findings.title: Sizing and projected-risk gate use closed balance; the EA uses ACCOUNT_EQUITY for both
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:534 (risk_money = balance * risk_pct), 543 (projected = balance - ...); vs FTMOQuantEA.mq5:691 (riskMoney = ACCOUNT_EQUITY * pct) and 435-436 (projectedEquity = ACCOUNT_EQUITY - ...)
confirmed_findings.claim: try_open() sizes risk_money from the closed-trade balance and gates projected risk against balance, but the EA it mirrors sizes from ACCOUNT_EQUITY and gates ProjectedRiskAllowed() against equity. Pyramid adds by construction happen while units are open with floating PnL (post-TP1, usually floating profit), so the harness systematically under-sizes adds relative to the live EA in winning trends and over-sizes relative to it under floating losses; guard proximity is likewise measured from a different base.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Dollar PnL, compounding, drawdown and soft-guard trigger frequency all diverge from what the live EA would produce; in profitable trends the harness understates the EA's add size (understating both its profits and its risk), under floating losses it overstates size.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Verified all four cited locations. Harness line 534 sizes risk_money from `balance` and line 543 gates projected risk from `balance`; `balance` is only updated on realized closes in book() (line 484), never marked to market. The EA sizes riskMoney from ACCOUNT_EQUITY (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:691-692) and gates ProjectedRiskAllowed against ACCOUNT_EQUITY (435-436). The divergence is live, not theoretical: pyramid adds (backtest lines 711-733) call try_open while units are open with floating PnL — and because stops are processed earlier in the same bar, surviving tp1-done runners are necessarily on the profitable side of entry at add time, so equity > balance in exactly the winning-trend scenario. This is not a disclosed limitation: the docstring (lines 2-9) explicitly claims to mirror the EA's sizing and guard logic, and the harness demonstrably can compute mark-to-market equity (it does so at lines 605-611 and 749-753 for other purposes). Fresh flat entries are unaffected (balance==equity when flat), and per-unit R stats are largely insulated, but dollar PnL, compounding, sizing of adds, and soft-guard proximity genuinely diverge from the EA, with impact direction mixed (understates EA add size in profitable trends, overstates under floating losses) — consistent with the claim's neutral_or_unknown label. Claim confirmed; not refutable.

confirmed_findings.title: max_trades_day counter excludes pyramid adds; the EA counts every DEAL_ENTRY_IN, so the harness allows fresh trends the live EA would block
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:701, 709 (entries_today incremented only on new-trend entries; pyramid branch 712-731 never increments); vs FTMOQuantEA.mq5:283-286, 1062-1064
confirmed_findings.claim: The harness increments entries_today only when a fresh trend is opened, and only checks it in the flat branch. The EA's TodayStrategyStats counts every opening deal including pyramid adds toward 'entries' and blocks a new trend at entries >= InpMaxTradesPerDay. With max_trades_day=2, a day with one fresh trend plus one add exhausts the EA's quota, but the harness would still permit a second fresh trend the same day.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: The harness trades fresh-trend signals more often than the live EA can, so measured trade frequency, compounding and net profit do not transfer to live at the measured rate; if the extra trades share the strategy's expectancy this flatters the backtest, otherwise sign is unknown.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, not refuted. Harness: entries_today is incremented only at ftmo_quant_backtest.py:709 inside the fresh-trend flat branch (checked at :701); the pyramid-add branch at :712-733 calls try_open without incrementing or checking entries_today (grep confirms lines 466/588/701/709 are the only occurrences). EA: TodayStrategyStats (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:267-299) counts every DEAL_ENTRY_IN/INOUT deal carrying the EA magic since day start — pyramid adds included, since all opens go through OpenUnit (:674) on the single trade object stamped with InpMagicNumber (:979) — and the flat branch blocks a new trend at entries >= InpMaxTradesPerDay (:1062-1065). With defaults (max_trades_day=2, pyramid_enabled=True), a day with one fresh trend + one TP1 pyramid add + a flatten leaves the EA at entries=2 (new trend blocked) while the harness sits at entries_today=1 and opens a second fresh trend. The harness therefore permits fresh-trend entries the live EA would refuse, precisely on strong trend days; trade frequency/compounding do not transfer. This is a genuine parity defect, not among the disclosed limitations (H1 granularity, constant spread, server-time, stop-first). Impact direction: neutral/unknown formally, inflating if the marginal trades share positive expectancy — as the claim states.

confirmed_findings.title: summarize() metrics are per-tranche, not per-round-turn: win rate structurally boosted by scale-outs, PF pulled toward 1, expectancy_r diluted by tranche count
confirmed_findings.location: Bot-EA/backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:492-504 (one Trade row per tranche), 349-364 (summarize), 769-772 (oos/yearly on same rows)
confirmed_findings.claim: Every TP1/TP2/runner/stop tranche is a separate Trade row, so 'trades', 'win_rate_pct', 'profit_factor' and 'expectancy_r' describe tranches. Any unit reaching +1R books a guaranteed TP1 win row even when the whole unit nets a loss (runner stopped below entry), inflating win rate; splitting a net-losing unit into a winning and a losing tranche adds equal amounts to gross profit and gross loss, pulling PF toward 1 (down for a winning system, up for a losing one); expectancy_r divides the unchanged sum of r by the larger tranche count, diluting per-unit expectancy.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Headline win_rate_pct is inflated and trade count overstated versus round-turn units; PF and expectancy_r are compressed toward neutral. net_profit and sum-of-R are unaffected. Direction differs per metric, so gate outcomes depend on which statistic is read.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED at the cited lines; not refutable. book() (ftmo_quant_backtest.py:477-505) emits one Trade row per booked tranche — called from stop (631), tp1 (642), tp2 (656), trail (685), and every flatten (521) — so a scale-out unit produces up to 3 rows vs 1 for a stop-out. summarize() (349-364) computes trades/wins/win_rate_pct/profit_factor/expectancy_r over these tranche rows, and oos/yearly (769-772) reuse the same rows. The module docstring (1-9) discloses H1 granularity, constant spread, and stop-first pessimism but not per-tranche accounting, so this is not a disclosed intentional limitation. Two sub-mechanics in the claim are imprecise but do not refute it: (1) "unchanged sum of r" is false — unit_risk is pro-rated by close_lots/original_lots (487-491), so each tranche r (500) is the full R-multiple of its exit, and per-tranche expectancy_r is typically INFLATED, not diluted (worked example with defaults: winner unit rows r≈+0.909/+2.0/0 plus one stop-out row −0.909 gives reported expectancy_r=+0.5R while true per-unit expectancy is 0.0R — worse than claimed for a gate statistic); (2) after TP1 the stop moves to entry (644) and stops fill at unit.stop (631), so a net-losing unit with a booked TP1 win arises only via flatten paths (trend_change books at bar.open, soft_guard at adverse price), a narrower but real scenario. The PF-toward-1 arithmetic is correct for the dollar PF (350-359): splitting a net-losing unit adds equal amounts to gross profit and gross loss. Trade-count overstatement is trivially true; net_profit/ending_balance/drawdowns are unaffected. Core defect stands: headline win_rate_pct, trades, PF, and especially expectancy_r describe tranches, not round-turn units, and gate outcomes depend on which statistic is read.

confirmed_findings.title: ATR method mismatch: Python Wilder ATR vs EA iATR (SMA of True Range)
confirmed_findings.claim: The Python harness computes Wilder-smoothed ATR (recursive (period-1)/period smoothing), but the EA uses MT5's built-in iATR, which is a rolling simple average of True Range (ATR[i]=ATR[i-1]+(TR[i]-TR[i-period])/period). For period 14 these series diverge materially bar-to-bar (Wilder is roughly as smooth as a 27-period SMA). ATR drives the stop distance (line 531), the entry buffer that gates every breakout signal (lines 269-273), TP1/TP2 levels via initial_risk, the trailing distance (lines 674-676), pullback arming (lines 739, 743), and the volatility-regime ratio (line 441).
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Every trade's existence (buffer + vol gate), size (stop distance), and exit geometry differs from what the EA would do on identical data. The program's prior EA audit found this exact iATR-vs-Wilder mismatch changed roughly one third of signals on a sibling system, so the screen is not measuring the EA as shipped.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: CONFIRMED, could not refute. (1) Python side verified: backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py:190-205 implements textbook Wilder ATR — seed SMA at index period-1 (line 202), then recursive smoothing output[i] = ((period-1)*output[i-1] + tr)/period (line 204). Line 398 binds this series to every ATR-dependent decision exactly as the claim lists: entry buffer gating each breakout signal (lines 269-273), volatility-regime ratio (lines 438-441, numerator atr[prev]), stop distance (line 531), trailing distance (lines 674-676), and pullback re-arm (lines 739, 743). (2) EA side verified: experts/FTMOQuantEA.mq5:954 creates atrHandle = iATR(...), and grep shows that handle feeds the identical decision set (pullback arm 458-481, vol regime 552-562, entry buffer 611-614, stop distance 684-689, trail 739/855-857) — there is no custom ATR in the EA. MT5's built-in iATR is a rolling simple average of True Range (the standard ATR.mq5 update ATR[i]=ATR[i-1]+(TR[i]-TR[i-period])/period), not Wilder smoothing; this exact iATR-SMA-vs-Wilder divergence was independently confirmed in this program's own 38-agent MomentumPullbackEA audit (2026-07-10), where it changed roughly one third of signals on a sibling system, so materiality is established, not speculative (Wilder alpha 1/14 smooths like a ~27-period SMA, so the two series differ bar-to-bar at the margins where the 0.5-ATR buffer, vol-ratio bounds, and pullback threshold decide trade existence). (3) Not a disclosed limitation: the module docstring (lines 2-9) discloses only H1 aggregation and stop-first intrabar pessimism, and a repo-wide grep for Wilder/iATR/smoothing finds no acknowledgment of the method mismatch in README.md, docs/VALIDATION.md, docs/BACKTEST_RESULTS.md, or AGENTS.md. The TR definition itself matches (MT5's MathMax(high,prevClose)-MathMin(low,prevClose) equals the Python max-of-three), so the defect is purely the smoothing method — which is exactly what the claim states. Direction is correctly neutral/unknown: neither smoothing systematically flatters the strategy; the harness simply measures a different system than the EA as shipped.

confirmed_findings.title: Pullback/pyramid tracking runs on every bar in Python but only on gated in-session bars in the EA
confirmed_findings.claim: Python folds every H1 bar (including all overnight bars 16:00-06:00, the hour-11 bar orphaned by the skip-hour, and bars on locked or max-losses days) into trend_extreme and pullback arming. The EA's UpdatePullback only executes on the first tick of a new bar that survives the session gate (mq5:1046), the losses gate (mq5:1051), and the accountSafe gate, and it reads only the shift-1 bar — so with defaults it observes only the bars opening at hours 7-10 and 12-15, never overnight extremes. Because arming is monotone in observed data (higher trend_extreme and more observed lows both make 'ext - low >= 0.5*ATR' easier), Python arms strictly more pyramid re-entries than the EA can.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Pyramid adds — a core, default-on component of the strategy — fire in the screen from overnight pullbacks the live EA will never see. The screened P&L contains add-unit trades the EA cannot replicate; if adds are net-positive in the screen (the design intent), the screen overstates the EA, and it also overstates add-unit risk exposure on the FTMO daily-loss stats either way.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
CONFIRMED, not refuted. I traced both code paths concretely.

Python side (ftmo_quant_backtest.py:736-744): the tracking block `if units and trend_side != 0 and math.isfinite(atr[index]):` sits at the top level of the per-bar loop, after the entry blocks, with no session/losses/guard condition. Since positions are held overnight (the only flattens are trend_change at 593-598, Friday weekend at 600-601, soft_guard at 616-621, and stops/trails), every H1 bar while units are open — including bars opening 17:00-07:00, hour 12's neighbors, and bars on max-losses or profit-locked days — folds its high/low into trend_extreme and can set pullback_armed=True.

EA side (FTMOQuantEA.mq5): UpdatePullback (453-484) is called from exactly one place, OnTick line 1060. The call is preceded by `if(!accountSafe || !IsTradingSession()) return;` (1046-1047), the losses gate `if(losses >= InpMaxLosingTradesPerDay) return;` (1049-1052), and the new-bar latch (1054-1057). Crucially, `lastSignalBar = bar` (1057) executes only AFTER the gates, and UpdatePullback reads only shift-1 data (iHigh/iLow shift 1 at 461-462, ATR shift 1 at 458) — there is no catch-up loop over skipped bars, and OnTimer (1011-1016) never calls it. Tracing with defaults (session 8-17, skip hour 12, Friday close 17): processing ticks occur during hours 8,9,10,11,13,14,15,16, so the shift-1 bars ever observed are those opening at hours 7,8,9,10 and 12,13,14,15. The hour-11 bar is orphaned (hour 12 is skipped, and by hour 13 it is shift 2), and bars opening 16:00 through 06:00 are never observed. The claim's characterization is exact.

Monotonicity holds: for longs, trend_extreme is a running max of observed highs, and arming requires ext - observed_low >= pullback_atr*ATR; observing strictly more bars (overnight highs raise ext; overnight lows provide extra arming opportunities) can only arm earlier/more often, never later. Both sides reset identically on add (Python 731-733 resets armed+extreme; EA 1093-1096), so no offsetting effect. Python's add ENTRIES are still session-gated via entry_ready (690-698), matching the EA, but the ARMING state feeding those entries is computed from bars the EA can never see — so the Python screen fires pyramid adds (a default-on component, pyramid_enabled=True, max_units=3) on setups the live EA cannot take, and conversely never misses ones the EA takes.

Refutation angles checked and rejected: (a) not among the disclosed limitations (docstring lines 4-8 discloses H1 granularity, conservatism of intrabar resolution; the module explicitly claims to "mirror the EA's ... session ... logic", which this violates); (b) no alternate EA path updates trend_ext/pullback (grep confirms only lines 1060/1070/1095 call sites); (c) the skip-hour bar-12 case does NOT orphan bar 12 (it is shift-1 at hour 13) but DOES orphan bar 11, exactly as claimed. Direction of P&L impact is genuinely unknown (depends on whether the extra adds are net positive in the screen), but it is a real parity divergence in a core default-on mechanism, and it overstates add-unit exposure in the FTMO daily-loss statistics relative to what the EA would produce. The prior auditor's claim is accurate at every checkable detail.

confirmed_findings.title: Max-trades-per-day counter excludes pyramid adds in Python but the EA counts every entry deal
confirmed_findings.claim: Python increments entries_today only for fresh trend entries (line 709); pyramid adds (lines 711-733) are never counted. The EA's TodayStrategyStats counts every DEAL_ENTRY_IN with its magic number — pyramid adds included — and blocks fresh trend entries once the count reaches InpMaxTradesPerDay=2 (mq5:1064). So on any day with one trend entry plus at least one add, the EA is locked out of a second fresh trend entry, while Python (entries_today=1 < 2) will still take it.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: The screen takes fresh trend entries on multi-unit days that the live EA would refuse, so the trade population differs from the EA's on exactly the most active (trending) days. Extra trades of unknown sign are attributed to the EA.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
The claim is CONFIRMED by concrete reading of both files; I could not refute it.

EA side (experts/FTMOQuantEA.mq5): TodayStrategyStats (lines 267-299) iterates all history deals since TradingDayStart and, filtering only on DEAL_MAGIC == InpMagicNumber (line 280), increments `entries` for every DEAL_ENTRY_IN or DEAL_ENTRY_INOUT deal (lines 283-286). trade.SetExpertMagicNumber(InpMagicNumber) at line 979 means every OpenUnit fill carries that magic — including pyramid adds, which go through the same OpenUnit at line 1093. So on a day with one fresh trend entry plus one pyramid add, the EA's `entries` count is 2. In OnTick, when flat (units==0), line 1064 blocks a new fresh entry if `entries >= InpMaxTradesPerDay` (default 2, line 42). The pyramid path itself (lines 1077-1097) never checks `entries`, so adds are uncapped by this counter in the EA too — the divergence is specifically on fresh entries after an add.

Python side (backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py): `entries_today` is incremented only at line 709, inside the fresh-trend-entry branch gated by `entries_today < config.max_trades_day` at line 701 (default max_trades_day=2, line 100). The pyramid-add branch (lines 711-733) calls try_open at line 731 but never touches entries_today. Both sides reset the counter at the trading-day boundary (py:588; EA via HistorySelect from TradingDayStart), so the reset is at parity — only the counting of adds diverges.

Concrete divergent execution: day with fresh entry (both counters=1), TP1 hits, pullback add fills (EA history now has 2 IN deals; Python entries_today still 1), then all units exit intraday (trend-change flatten mq5:1033-1043 / stop / trail — all can occur same day), then a new signal fires while flat: EA at line 1064 sees entries=2 >= 2 and refuses; Python at line 701 sees entries_today=1 < 2 and opens a second fresh trend entry. The backtest therefore contains fresh entries on active/trending days that the live EA would never take. This is not among the disclosed intentional limitations (H1 granularity, constant spread, server-time timestamps, stop-first pessimism). Impact direction is genuinely unknown (the extra trades' sign is not determined a priori), matching the claimant's neutral_or_unknown label — but as a parity defect it is real.

confirmed_findings.title: H4 confluence is one H4 bar staler than the EA at H4-boundary entry hours (08:00, 16:00)
confirmed_findings.claim: context_ok evaluates the HTF stack at prev = index-1 and htf_ema_aligned returns the EMA of bucket(prev)-1. When the entry bar opens exactly on an H4 boundary (08:00 and 16:00 server, both tradable session hours), the previous H1 bar belongs to the just-completed H4 bucket, so bucket(prev)-1 is two H4 bars back — but the EA at that same decision tick reads H4 shift 1, the just-completed H4 bar. Python's H4 EMA input is one full H4 bar older than the EA's for 2 of the 8 tradable entry hours. (D1 is unaffected because the day boundary falls outside the session.)
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: Roughly a quarter of potential entry decisions apply a stale H4 EMA stack, admitting breakouts the EA would reject and rejecting ones it would take whenever the H4 fast/slow relationship changed in the latest H4 bar — precisely the moments a trend system trades.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning:
The claim is CONFIRMED by concrete trace of both codebases; I could not refute it.

Python side (backtest/ftmo_quant_backtest.py): context_ok (lines 419-427) evaluates the HTF stack at prev = index - 1 and reads htf_fast_al[prev]/htf_slow_al[prev]. htf_ema_aligned (lines 231-248) keys each H1 bar to its H4 bucket via hour // factor (factor=4 → buckets start at 00/04/08/12/16/20) and returns htf_fast[bucket - 1], i.e. the EMA as of the close of the H4 bucket BEFORE the one containing that H1 bar.

EA side (experts/FTMOQuantEA.mq5): entries are gated to the first tick of a new H1 bar via lastSignalBar (lines 1054-1057), and ConfluenceOK → HtfAgrees reads IndicatorValue(handle, 1) (lines 534-535) — the last COMPLETED H4 bar at that tick.

Concrete trace at the 16:00 decision bar: EA at the first tick of 16:00 reads H4 shift 1 = the 12:00-15:59 H4 bar, which completed at that instant. Python: prev = the 15:00 H1 bar → bucket = 12:00-15:59 (15//4=3) → bucket-1 = 08:00-11:59; Python uses the EMA as of the close of the 08:00 H4 bar — exactly one full H4 bar staler than the EA. Same at 08:00 (Python reads the 00:00-bucket close; EA reads the 04:00-07:59 bar). At non-boundary hours (9,10,11,13,14,15) prev lies in the same H4 bucket as index and bucket(prev)-1 equals the EA's shift-1 bar, so parity holds there — confirming the defect is specific to boundary hours. The parity-correct form is htf_fast_al[index] (bucket(index)-1), which equals the EA's read at ALL hours and is still fully completed data at the bar-index open, so the extra staleness is not required to avoid look-ahead; the docstring's anti-lookahead rationale (lines 225-227) does not cover it.

Claim's caveats also verify: tradable entry hours are 8,9,10,11,13,14,15,16 (session 8-17 minus skip_hours=(12,), lines 102-108, in_session lines 312-323), so 08:00 and 16:00 are 2 of 8 ≈ 25% of entry hours. D1 (htf2_factor=24) buckets by day; the midnight boundary is outside the session so prev is always in the same day-bucket as index — unaffected, as claimed. This is not among the disclosed intentional limitations (H1 OHLC granularity, constant spread, server-time timestamps, stop-first pessimism). Direction is genuinely neutral/unknown: the stale H4 stack can both admit breakouts the EA would reject and reject ones it would take, specifically when the H4 fast/slow relationship changed in the latest H4 bar.

confirmed_findings.title: EMA warmup: dataset-seeded EMAs and ungated HTF stacks vs the EA's full-history indicators
confirmed_findings.claim: Python seeds every EMA with the first value of the dataset (line 184) and exposes HTF EMA values from the second higher-timeframe bucket onward with no minimum-sample gate (lines 244-248 only require bucket-1 >= 0; the isfinite check at 423/431 passes almost immediately). Entries unlock at only max(ema_slow+10, donchian+2)=210 H1 bars (line 260), at which point the slow H1 EMA200 still carries ~12% seed weight, the 'H4 EMA200' is an EMA over ~52 H4 closes, and the 'D1 EMA200' is an EMA over roughly 9-13 daily closes. The EA's iMA handles compute over the terminal's full multi-year history and are fully converged.
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: For the first months (H1/H4) up to roughly the first one to two years (D1 EMA200) of the sample, the trend filter and both confluence gates are not the EA's indicators at all — a large early fraction of the in-sample trade population can differ from what the EA would have produced, contaminating in-sample stats and, via the 70/30 split, the baseline the OOS is compared against.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Confirmed at every cited location. (1) ftmo_quant_backtest.py:184 seeds every EMA with values[0]; at the first tradable index (210, per the gate at line 260: max(ema_slow+10, donchian+2)=210) the signal reads slow[209], which carries (1-2/201)^209 = 12.4% seed weight — the claim's ~12% is exact. (2) htf_ema_aligned lines 244-248 expose HTF EMA values from the second HTF bucket onward (bucket-1 >= 0) with no minimum-sample gate; the only downstream guards are isfinite checks at lines 423/431, which pass immediately. At bar 210 the 'H4 EMA200' is an EMA over ~52 H4 closes (210/4=52.5) and the 'D1 EMA200' (calendar-day buckets via key (y,m,d,hour//24) at line 232) over ~9 daily closes — the claim's 52 and 9-13 figures check out. (3) The EA (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:950-976) creates iMA handles on the signal TF plus both HTF timeframes, computed by the terminal over full multi-year history and hence converged. EMA200 needs ~462 samples for <1% seed weight, so the Python H1 stack diverges materially until ~bar 462, the H4 stack for ~15 trading weeks, and the D1 stack for ~1.8 years of trading days — all inside the 70% in-sample region (split at line 399, oos flag at line 502), contaminating the IS trade population and the baseline OOS is compared against, exactly as alleged. It is not a disclosed limitation (the docstring discloses only H1 granularity, constant spread, server-time assumption, and stop-first pessimism, and claims to 'mirror the EA's default signal' logic), and the neutral/unknown direction label is appropriate since an unconverged EMA200 hugs price and can either admit or block trades the converged EA gate would decide differently.

confirmed_findings.title: Daily lock semantics: EA latches trading off for the day; Python re-arms the same day
confirmed_findings.claim: Three related lock divergences: (a) the EA's daily profit lock latches tradingLocked for the whole trading day (mq5:361-367 persists lock_day), while Python re-evaluates 'balance - day_start_balance < 1%' each bar (690-694), so if profit is given back Python resumes trading the same day; (b) after a soft-guard breach the EA's EmergencyFlatten latches the day locked (mq5:301-341), while Python's soft_guard flatten (616-621) applies no day lock — with losses_today still below the cap and the projected-risk gate passing, Python can re-enter the same day, even the same bar; (c) while locked the EA skips the trend-flip flatten (mq5:1033 requires accountSafe) and holds units to their stops, while Python flattens on flips unconditionally (593-598).
confirmed_findings.impact_on_results: The days on which these paths diverge are exactly the tail days that determine the FTMO survival outputs (max_daily_equity_loss_pct, official_rule_breach, soft_guard_exits). Python both trades when the EA would be locked and exits flips the EA would ride, so breach/drawdown statistics do not reflect EA behavior on stressed days.
confirmed_findings.verify_reasoning: Verified against both files. Sub-claim (a) CONFIRMED: the EA latches tradingLocked for the whole trading day when TodayClosedPnl() >= initialBalance*InpDailyProfitLockPct/100 (FTMOQuantEA.mq5:361-367, persisted via lock_day; cleared only by RefreshDailyState on a new dayId at mq5:140/162-164), while Python has no lock state and re-evaluates 'balance - day_start_balance < initial*1%' fresh every bar (ftmo_quant_backtest.py:690-694). Concrete divergence path: intraday closed PnL crosses +1% (e.g., three pyramided units booking TP1+TP2 at ~0.34% each), latching the EA; a later full-stop loss on a pyramid unit (~-0.32%) pulls Python's day PnL back under the threshold and Python takes a fresh same-day entry the EA would refuse. Sub-claim (c) CONFIRMED: mq5:1033 gates the trend-flip flatten on accountSafe (= !tradingLocked per mq5:368) while ManagePositions (mq5:1022) still runs, so a profit-locked EA holds an open runner through an EMA flip to its stop/trail; Python flattens on the flip unconditionally (py:593-598). This divergence requires only 'profit lock trips with a runner open, then an EMA flip same day' — realistically reachable, and it lands exactly on the profit-lock tail days that drive max_daily_equity_loss_pct / official_rule_breach / give-back statistics. Sub-claim (b) REFUTED in mechanism: after the soft_guard flatten (py:616-621, adverse=True) exits are booked at the same adverse prices used to compute adverse_equity (py:514-521 vs 605-611, plus an extra commission side), so post-flatten balance <= adverse_equity <= active_floor; balance is then constant while flat and active_floor is constant for the rest of the day (py:326-332 uses only day_start_balance and initial_balance), so try_open's projected-risk gate 'balance - risk_money*1.15 > active_floor' (py:543-547) fails for every entry/pyramid attempt for the remainder of the day — the claim's required 'projected-risk gate passing' cannot occur; the gate is a de-facto same-day lock matching the EA, and both re-arm the next day (mq5:162-166 with emergencyMode cleared at mq5:339 once flat). Overall: 2 of 3 sub-claims are genuine, line-grounded lock-semantics divergences between Python and the EA on stressed/profit-lock days, so the finding as a whole stands (refuted=false), with the correction that the soft-guard same-day re-entry (b) is impossible due to the projected-risk gate. Direction: neutral/unknown as claimed — Python both trades on days the EA is locked (a) and exits flips the EA would ride (c), so FTMO survival outputs do not reflect EA behavior on those days but the sign of the bias is not determined.
